classification.difficultyReason: Parts a and b are direct applications of the cylinder and cone formulas, and part c is a simple ratio. Part d asks the student to see that the 1/3 relationship holds for any equal base and height, which is a small step of interpretation. That puts it above the routine formula substitutions in p4-q2. It is below p6-q7, which needs two different solids, a diameter-to-radius step and a difference to be found.

content.prompt: A cone and a cylinder have the same base and the same perpendicular height.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the volume of the cylinder. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the volume of the cone. Round your answer to 2 decimal places.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What fraction of the volume of the cylinder is the volume of the cone?

children.label: d
children.prompt: A different cone and cylinder have the same base radius of $2.5\,\mathrm{m}$ and the same perpendicular height of $9\,\mathrm{m}$. What fraction of the volume of the cylinder is the volume of the cone?
